standard.title: Analyse texts using metalanguage
standard.description: analyse a range of Chinese texts, using metalanguage to explain linguistic, textual and cultural elements
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can compare language structures and features across target language and English using metalanguage (AC9LCH8EU03). They have applied comparative metalanguage to text types and genre conventions. They have not yet conducted full stylistic analysis of target language texts, examined essay organisation conventions specific to the target language, analysed language in media contexts, or described genres unique to the target language literary tradition.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students analyse a range of target language texts using metalanguage to explain linguistic, textual and cultural elements — including stylistic devices, genre organisation, content structure, and culturally-specific literary forms.

nodes.label: Stylistic and linguistic analysis
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify and analyse grammatical differences between languages using metalanguage, and analyse language in a range of text types for purpose and audience.
nodes.minimum_width: Use metalanguage to analyse at least three linguistic features in a target language text, and compare at least one feature with its English equivalent.
nodes.typical_width: Use metalanguage to identify grammatical differences across languages — word order, verb mood, tense, possessive pronouns; analyse sequence of content in different text types; explain use of data and evidence in texts; analyse language in emails, blogs, news articles for purpose differences; identify linguistic terms in media reporting.
wider: Produce a full linguistic and textual analysis of a target language text — annotating every feature with metalanguage and explaining its contribution to the text's purpose
Compare how the same linguistic feature operates across formal and informal registers in the target language — explain the difference and discuss the cultural logic behind it
nodes.hinge_reason: Linguistic and textual analysis using metalanguage is the prerequisite for all sophisticated text engagement at Y9-10. Students who cannot name and analyse language features cannot produce the analytical responses the descriptor requires.

response_modes.reason: Metalanguage for analysis is built through repeated deployment across varied text types. Students need to encounter and apply each metalanguage term across multiple text analysis contexts before it becomes functional analytical vocabulary.

success_criteria: Uses metalanguage to analyse at least three linguistic features in a target language text
Compares at least one feature with its English equivalent

nodes.label: Genre organisation and essay conventions
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can analyse how content is structured in target language text types — including essay organisation conventions — and compare these with English equivalents.
nodes.minimum_width: Analyse the content organisation of at least two target language text types and compare with English conventions for at least one, identifying at least two differences.
nodes.typical_width: Analyse the sequence of content in different text types; examine how ideas are ordered and substantiated across genres and languages; compare essay organisation — where the author's position appears, how evidence is marshalled; analyse magazine and online text layout; compare literature across languages and cultures.
wider: Compare essay organisation conventions in the target language with English — explain the cultural logic behind each organisation pattern and discuss implications for bilingual academic writing
Apply target language essay organisation conventions in an original piece — then compare with a parallel English essay on the same topic

response_modes.reason: Genre organisation analysis requires students to compare across text types and languages systematically. Explicit organisational framework analysis — identifying where position appears, how evidence is structured — builds the comparative capacity before students can analyse independently.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Understanding how target language essay and argument structure differs from English is a genuinely valuable academic insight for background language learner entry students who write in both languages. Width investment here builds bilingual academic literacy with direct transfer value.
success_criteria: Analyses content organisation in at least two target language text types
Compares with English conventions for at least one, identifying at least two differences

nodes.label: Literary and cultural text analysis
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can analyse stylistic devices in literary texts, describe target language-specific literary forms, and explain the cultural elements embedded in literary and cultural texts.
nodes.minimum_width: Analyse at least two stylistic devices in a target language literary text using metalanguage, and describe at least one genre or form specific to the target language literary tradition.
nodes.typical_width: Analyse stylistic writing techniques in target language; examine the four-step essay composition tradition; explore literary language differences from everyday text; analyse how magic and danger are portrayed in folk legends across cultures; analyse traditional Chinese literary forms and their origins.
wider: Produce a full stylistic analysis of a target language literary text — annotating every stylistic device and evaluating the text's cultural and literary significance

Research a specific target language literary form — describe its conventions, trace its historical origins, and explain its cultural significance in relation to contemporary target language literature

response_modes.reason: Literary and cultural text analysis integrates linguistic analysis (node 1) and genre organisation understanding (node 2) into a full cultural-literary analytical act. The teaching investment is in creating genuine engagement with the target language literary tradition — students as culturally-informed readers and analysts.

success_criteria: Analyses at least two stylistic devices in a literary text using metalanguage
Describes at least one genre or form specific to the target language literary tradition
